pages.title: Altavas
pages.description: municipality of the Philippines in the province of Aklan
pages.extract: Altavas is a 4th class municipality in the province of Aklan, Philippines.

pages.title: Budva Riviera
pages.extract: The Budva Riviera is the main tourist drag in Montenegro.

pages.title: Crosby
pages.description: town in the Metropolitan Borough of Sefton, in Merseyside, England

pages.title: Francestown
pages.extract: Francestown is a town in New Hampshire. The 2010 census put the population at 1562.

pages.title: Longyan
pages.extract: Longyan (龙岩; Lóngyán) is an inland city in western Fujian, China. For travellers, it is best known as a gateway to the Hakka tulou of Yongding and other rural areas of western Fujian. The city itself is less tourist-oriented than coastal destinations such as Xiamen, but it can be used as a base for exploring the surrounding region.

pages.title: Mons
pages.extract: Mons (Dutch: Bergen, not to be confused with the namesake city in Norway) is the capital of the Belgian province of Hainaut, in the region of Wallonia. The town is a worthy place to base yourself for a multi-day exploration of the Hainaut region.

pages.title: Paro
pages.extract: Paro (population 11,500 in 2017) is a town in the south west of Bhutan.

pages.title: Waldo County
pages.extract: Waldo County which borders Maine's Penobscot Bay on the Atlantic Ocean is divided between the more populated coast and the interior highlands.

pages.title: Zipolite
pages.description: beach destination along the Pacific Coast of Oaxaca, Mexico
pages.extract:
Zipolite is a growing backpacker beach destination along the south-western Pacific coast of Oaxaca, Mexico. It is famous as Mexico's only officially-sanctioned nude beach.
A new highway built in 2024 has cut the travel time from Oaxaca in half, now only 4 hours by bus. The rapidly-growing Huatulco airport is one hour away and a popular choice for accessing the Oaxacan coast.

pages.title: Dubai/Jebel Ali
pages.description: port town in the United Arab Emirates

pages.extract:
There is more than one place called Yulin:

Yulin (Guangxi) (玉林市) — a town in China
Yulin (Shaanxi) (榆林市) — also in China

pages.title: Spata
pages.extract: Spata is mostly a residential town (about 10.000 people) and in many ways as a suburb of Athens, which lies 20km to the west. Athens International Airport is situated on Spata grounds and sometimes referred to as Spata Airport. The town is also home to one of the largest zoos in Greece: Attica Zoological Park.

pages.title: Lobamba
pages.extract: Lobamba is the traditional capital of Eswatini, and home to around 11,000 citizens.

pages.title: Kosciuszko National Park
pages.description: National Park in New South Wales, Australia
pages.extract: Kosciuszko National Park is in the Snowy Mountains of New South Wales and the largest national park in New South Wales, and the highest in Australia. The sunburned country isn't often associated with snow, but the park offers good skiing opportunities.

pages.title: Puerto Esperanza (Cuba)
pages.extract: Puerto Esperanza is a small seaside town in Pinar del Rio Province, just north of Viñales. The beach apparently is not Varadero but it's an authentically relaxed Cuban fishing town with very few foreign tourists.

pages.title: Driving in Spain
pages.extract: Driving in Spain can be a frustrating experience in the country's biggest cities, but a good idea to get to places off the beaten path.

pages.title: Strait Shores
pages.description: rural community in New Brunswick, Canada
pages.extract: Strait Shores is a rural area in Southeastern New Brunswick near the Nova Scotia border, fronting on the Northumberland Strait. The largest community in the area is the small village of Port Elgin.

pages.title: Haapajärvi
pages.description: town in the region of Northern Ostrobothnia in Finland

pages.title: Green Ribbon
pages.extract: Green Ribbon (Gröna Bandet) is a Swedish long-distance trek, which stretches from the southern border of the Scandinavian mountain range to Treriksröset, the tripoint where Sweden, Norway, and Finland meet. It covers approximately 1,300 km.

pages.title: Seongnam
pages.description: city in Gyeonggi Province, South Korea
